title: Annotatio IV §.XX: (1) They admit Waldensian confession unclear — thanksgiving/commemoration; Picard obscurity
pass_a_gloss: (1) yet is forced to confess that the Waldenses’ Confession which exists in Sleidanus Book 16 is less clear — namely that part clear enough that it could seem the same as the Lutheran — because they say: The Sacred Supper is a thanksgiving and a commemoration of the benefit received through Christ. Nay indeed Strauch forms his 10th Aphorism of the second chapter thus: Concerning the Lord’s Supper it is less certain what all (Waldenses) sense, and much less what they formerly sensed: For although the Picards seem to expound this article orthodoxly, yet others’ Confessions are more obscure than that Zwinglianism should lucidly appear condemned in the same.
pass_b_english: (1) Yet they must admit the Waldensian Confession in Sleidanus Book 16 is less clear than a Lutheran twin — it calls the Supper thanksgiving and commemoration of the benefit received through Christ.

Strauch’s Aphorism 10: less certain what all Waldenses sense, still less what they once sensed — Picards may look orthodox, but other confessions are too obscure for Zwinglianism to appear lucidly condemned.
source_text: (1) tamen fateri necesse habet, minus claram esse Waldensium Confessionem, quæ apud Sleidanum extet lib. 16. puta, eam in partem, claram, ut cum Lutherana videri possit eadem, quia dicunt: Esse S. Cœnam gratiarum actionem & beneficii per Christum accepti commemorationem. Imò verò Strauchius Aphorismum suum 10, capitis secundi, ita format: De Cœna Domini minùs certum est, quid omnes (Waldenses) sentiant, ac multo minus quid olim senserint: Quamvis enim Picardi orthodoxè articulum hunc exponere videantur, aliorum tamen Confessiones obscuriores sunt, quàm ut Zwinglianismum in iisdem damnari luculenter appareat.
